facts.statement: Caieiria is a genus of titanosaurian dinosaur found in the Late Cretaceous Serra da Galga Formation in Brazil.
facts.quote: Caieiria (named after the Caieira locality where its fossils were recovered) is a genus of titanosaurian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Serra da Galga Formation (formerly a unit of the Marília Formation) of Brazil.

facts.statement: The holotype of Caieiria consists of a series of ten caudal vertebrae identified as MCT 1719-R.
facts.quote: The describers of Trigonosaurus also referred a series of ten caudal vertebrae, MCT 1719-R, as the paratype of their new genus.

facts.statement: The species name allocaudata means "strange tail" and refers to the dinosaur's unusual tail anatomy.
facts.quote: The generic name "Caieiria" honors the Caieira locality while the specific name "allocaudata" means "strange tail", referring to its unusual anatomy.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Caieiria in a clade at the base of Aeolosaurini within the group Rinconsauria.
facts.quote: Both taxa were found to be in a clade at the base of Aeolosaurini, which, like many other analyses, is recovered within Rinconsauria.

facts.statement: Caieiria lived during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The paleoenvironment of Caieiria included other dinosaurs like Ypupiara and crocodylomorphs such as Itasuchus and Peirosaurus.
facts.quote: Other than Baurutitan and Caieiria, other animals from this formation include the unenlagiine Ypupiara and the crocodylomorphs Itasuchus, Peirosaurus, and Uberabasuchus.
